title: Defanging an IP Address
statement: You receive `address`, a well-formed IPv4 address (four numbers from 0 to 255 joined by dots). Produce its "defanged" form: the same text, except that each `.` is swapped for the three-character sequence `[.]`. Every other character stays as it is and in the same order.
constraints: address is a valid IPv4 address: four decimal numbers from 0 to 255, separated by single dots, without leading zeros
notes:
## Intuition

Nothing about the address needs to be understood: it is just text. Walk through it once and copy each character to a new string, writing `[.]` whenever the character is a dot. (A library one-liner such as splitting on `.` and joining with `[.]` does the same thing.)

## Approach

1. Start with an empty `result`.
2. Visit each character `ch` of `address` from left to right.
3. If `ch` is `.`, append `[.]`; otherwise append `ch` unchanged.
4. Return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`address = "1.1.1.1"`. The characters arrive as `1`, `.`, `1`, `.`, `1`, `.`, `1`. The digits are copied and each of the three dots becomes `[.]`, so `result` grows `"1"` → `"1[.]"` → `"1[.]1"` → ... → `"1[.]1[.]1[.]1"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n) for an address of n characters (at most 15), since each character is handled once.
- Space: O(n) for the output, which is exactly 6 characters longer than the input.

## Pitfalls

- In a regular expression `.` matches any character, so `address.replace(/./g, '[.]')` would defang every digit too; escape it as `/\./g`.
- `replace` with a plain string `'.'` changes only the first dot; use `replaceAll` or a global regex.
- Do not change the digits: `"10.0.0.255"` keeps its zeros exactly as written.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `result` | the defanged address built so far |
| `ch` | the character of `address` being copied |

narration.2: Begin with an empty output string.
narration.3: Look at the characters of the address one by one, left to right.
narration.4: A dot is the only character that needs changing.
narration.5: Write the bracketed dot in its place.
narration.10: Every character has been copied; return the defanged address.
